logicalBugs.explanation: Saving the Body field through its popup updates the stored body and field preview, but leaves the main Note or Task editor showing the old content. Editing that stale document then overwrites the completed popup save.

rootCause.explanation: RichTextFieldEditor memoizes initialBody by fieldName and recordId, creates its editor once, and only replaces editor content when recordId changes. External completed body saves do not refresh an already-mounted editor; its next save replaces the entire body with its stale document.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Saving the Body field through its popup updates the stored body and field preview, but leaves the main Note or Task editor showing the old content. Editing that stale document then overwrites the completed popup save.

sourceBugs.name: A stale Note or Task main editor overwrites completed Body-field saves

reproductionPaths.expected: After a Body-field edit is saved, the main editor reflects the saved content so subsequent edits preserve that change.
reproductionPaths.actual: The Body preview and a separately opened record show the new saved text, while the already-open main editor still shows the original body. Typing in that stale editor saves the old body plus the new typing, replacing the completed popup change. Reload confirms the newer popup text is lost. Both Notes and Tasks reproduce; popup-only and main-only save controls retain their changes.
reproSteps: Sign in, create a fresh Note with an initial body such as Original body, and allow that body to save.
Keep its main body editor open. Open the Body field’s edit popup, replace the body with Updated body, dismiss the popup, and allow the save to complete.
Observe the Body field preview showing Updated body while the main editor still shows Original body. Open the same record in a separate tab to confirm Updated body has already been saved.
Return to the original tab and type additional text in the stale main editor without refreshing or switching record tabs.
Allow that edit to save, then reload. Observe Original body plus the added text, with the completed Updated body change overwritten.
Repeat with a fresh Task. As a control, save a popup edit and reload without editing the stale main editor; the popup’s new body persists.

reproductionPaths.explanation: An already-open Body-field popover retains an old document and overwrites completed main-editor saves when edited.

sourceBugs.name: Editing a stale Body-field popover overwrites the main note's recently saved paragraph

reproductionPaths.expected: An untouched Body popover should reflect completed main-editor saves before a subsequent edit, preserving already-saved content.
reproductionPaths.actual: The main editor saves new text successfully, but an already-open Body popover remains stale. Editing that popover saves its older document and removes the main-editor additions; reload confirms persisted loss.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Note with an initial body and let it save.
Open its Body-field popover and keep it mounted.
Add distinctive text through the main body editor and wait for saving to finish. Confirm the new body through a separate tab or account.
Edit the still-open stale Body popover and allow its save to complete.
Reload the record and confirm the previously saved main-editor additions are gone.
Repeat with a Task. Control: open the popover only after the main-editor save; subsequent editing preserves both changes.

matchingGuidance.distinction: The existing entry covers a stale main editor overwriting a completed Body-popover save. This entry covers the reverse direction: an already-open stale Body popover overwrites a completed main-editor save.

limitations: Some reproduced insertions were within existing text rather than a final paragraph; confirmed saved-text loss does not depend on insertion position.
Other rich-text hosts and arbitrary user roles are not generalized.
Newer runtime was not tested.

logicalBugs.explanation: Pending Note or Task body edits are silently lost when the rich-text editor unmounts before its save delay, including opening the full record or leaving the body tab. Waiting for autosave preserves the same text.

rootCause.explanation: RichTextFieldEditor debounces document handling by 500ms and persistence by a further 300ms. It does not flush these callbacks on unmount, so opening another record or switching away from the body tab can discard the pending document before it reaches the server.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The note side panel does not flush pending body edits when Open navigates to the full record. Reproduced twice; waiting before Open preserves the content.

sourceBugs.name: Opening a new note immediately after typing permanently loses its body

reproductionPaths.expected: Open should preserve the body currently entered in the note side panel.
reproductionPaths.actual: The entered text is visible before Open, but the full note opens with an empty body. It remains empty after waiting and reloading.
reproSteps: Sign in and open Notes from the workspace navigation.
Click New Note.
Enter a unique note title such as QA Notes Quick Open Race and press Enter.
Type Expected body persists into the note body editor.
Immediately click Open at the side-panel footer.
Wait for the full note page to load, then reload it.
Observe the note body is empty and the entered content has been lost.

reproductionPaths.expected: Switching tabs should flush pending body edits or retain them until autosave completes.
reproductionPaths.actual: A newly appended paragraph vanishes on returning from Timeline and remains absent after reload. The report reproduces the loss on a standalone Note and a Task, with no warning.
reproSteps: Open a standalone Note or Task and enter body text, allowing it to save.
Append a new paragraph and immediately click Timeline.
Return to the body tab and observe that the appended paragraph is already missing.
Reload to confirm persistence loss. Repeat on the other activity type.

logicalBugs.explanation: Pressing Escape in record detail Currency or Address editors commits the pending draft instead of cancelling it and preserving the saved value.

rootCause.explanation: FieldWidgetInputContextProvider implements Escape by persisting the supplied newValue and then closing the editor, the same sequence as Enter. Currency and Address editors supply their pending drafts, so Escape commits instead of discarding them.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Pressing Escape in an Annual Revenue editor commits the pending amount instead of preserving the previously saved value.

reproductionPaths.actual: A saved EUR -250 amount became EUR 16 in both the field and Timeline after typing 1e6, which the input filtered to 16, and pressing Escape.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Company and save Annual Revenue as EUR -250.
Reopen Annual Revenue and replace the amount by typing 1e6; observe that the input contains 16.
Press Escape to close the editor.
Observe EUR 16 in the field and its Timeline update instead of the previous EUR -250.

limitations: The accepted defect is Escape committing the pending edit. Scientific-notation support is not claimed.

reproSteps: Create a fresh Company and save Address as 17 QA Avenue, Montréal, Québec, H2Y 1C6, Canada.
Reopen Address and replace Address 1 with CANCELLED STREET.
Press Escape to close the editor.
Observe that the changed street was saved in the Address field and activity Timeline.

logicalBugs.explanation: Opening another company’s Notes or Tasks in the side panel overwrites the main company’s activity header and makes its New action create records linked only to the side-panel company.

rootCause.explanation: Widget header state is keyed by object-level pageLayoutId and widget ID rather than record or mounted publisher. Main-page and side-panel activities overwrite one another’s count and creation callback, and one publisher cleanup can clear the other surface’s header.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Opening another company’s Notes or Tasks in the side panel overwrites the main company’s activity header and makes its New action create records linked only to the side-panel company.

Open A on its full record page and select Notes.
Open B in the side panel and select Notes.
Click New in A’s main Notes header, save a uniquely named note, reload and inspect its company relation: it links only to B.
Repeat with Tasks on both records; New from A’s main Tasks header also targets B.
Control: creating from A without a side panel, or with B’s side panel on Home, targets A correctly.

rootCause.explanation: The preview helper returns the first nonempty inline text item rather than concatenating the paragraph and traversing link inline content. Formatting splits and link nodes can therefore drop saved text from the displayed preview.

logicalBugs.explanation: Restoring a deleted Note or Task reactivates relations removed before deletion. If a relation was removed and re-added beforehand, Restore can revive both link rows and show duplicate activity cards.

rootCause.explanation: Note and Task restore hooks restore every soft-deleted target row by activity ID, without recording which targets were live at activity deletion. Previously unlinked rows and multiple historical links are therefore restored together.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Restoring a deleted Note or Task reactivates relations removed before deletion. If a relation was removed and re-added beforehand, Restore can revive both link rows and show duplicate activity cards.

sourceBugs.name: Restoring Notes or Tasks revives removed relations and can create duplicate links

reproductionPaths.expected: Restoring a Note or Task restores the relations present when it was deleted and leaves previously removed relations absent.
reproductionPaths.actual: A relation removed from a Note or Task and confirmed absent after reload returns after Delete and Restore, and persists after another reload. When another relation was retained, Restore brought back both the retained relation and the previously removed relation. When the same company relation is removed and re-added before deleting and restoring a Note or Task, two live links for that activity/company pair can return. The company then displays duplicate cards for the same activity and an inflated total that persists after reload.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a fresh Task. Open its full record.
Use Relations to link an existing person, then dismiss the picker to save.
Reopen Relations, uncheck that person, dismiss the picker and reload. Confirm the relation is absent.
Use the command menu to delete the Task, then choose Restore in the deleted-record banner.
Observe that the previously removed person relation returns. Reload and confirm it remains.
Repeat with a fresh Note and a company relation: link the company, unlink it, confirm its absence after reload, then delete and restore the Note.
For the duplicate-card variant, create two distinct Notes related to a fresh company. On one Note, remove its company relation and then re-add the same company.
Delete that Note, open it through the company Timeline, and choose Restore.

Return to the company Notes tab. Observe two cards for the restored Note alongside the untouched Note, producing Notes 3. Reload and confirm the duplicates persist. The same remove/re-add, delete and restore sequence also reproduces for Tasks.

logicalBugs.explanation: After deleting a named Task or Note created from a company, its creation entry remains in the company Timeline but identifies the activity as Untitled.

rootCause.explanation: Timeline activity names are read from the live activity cache with linkedRecordCachedName as fallback. Creation can record an empty cached name before the user names the activity; deleting the activity removes the live title, exposing the empty fallback as Untitled.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After deleting a named Task or Note created from a company, its creation entry remains in the company Timeline but identifies the activity as Untitled.

sourceBugs.name: Deleting a named related Task or Note changes its creation Timeline label to Untitled

reproductionPaths.expected: After a named related Task or Note is deleted, its creation entry should either be removed from the Timeline or retain the activity’s saved name.
reproductionPaths.actual: After deletion and reload, the creation entry reads “You created a related task Untitled” or the equivalent for a Note. Opening the entry still reveals the correct deleted activity with its saved title and body. An undeleted control retains its name in the Timeline.
reproSteps: Sign in and open an existing company. From its Tasks tab, create a fresh related Task with a unique title, confirm the title with Enter, and enter body text.
Create a second named related Task in the same way and leave it undeleted as a control.
Open the first Task’s full record and use the command menu to delete it.
Return to the company, open Timeline, and reload.
Observe that the deleted Task’s creation entry remains but shows Untitled, while the undeleted Task’s entry retains its name.
Open the Untitled entry and confirm that the deleted Task still has its saved title and body.
Repeat with a fresh named related Note created from the company’s Notes tab; its creation entry also becomes Untitled after deletion and reload.

logicalBugs.explanation: Reloading a newly created Note or Task can reopen its title editor with an empty draft. Committing that draft erases the saved title; the Note variant also occurs when reopening the activity from its company Timeline after the creation-page reload.

rootCause.explanation: The creation flag retained in router history reopens the new-record title editor after reload. useOpenNewRecordTitleCell initializes its draft from the record store before the fetched title is available; commit handlers persist this empty draft.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Reloading a newly created Note or Task can reopen its title editor with an empty draft. Committing that draft erases the saved title; the Note variant also occurs when reopening the activity from its company Timeline after the creation-page reload.

sourceBugs.name: Refreshing newly created Notes or Tasks opens an empty title editor that can erase their saved names

reproductionPaths.expected: Reloading or reopening a named Note or Task preserves its saved title unless the user deliberately changes it.
reproductionPaths.actual: After the creation-page reload, the title editor can appear empty although the saved name initially remains in the browser title and can be recovered by pressing Escape. Clicking outside the editor, selecting Fields, or pressing Enter can instead persist the empty title. The activity then remains unnamed after reload. The Note’s saved body survives. Controls without the creation-page reload retain their titles.
reproSteps: For the Note variant, sign in and use a mobile-width viewport. Open a company’s full record, then choose More > Notes > New note.
Enter a unique title, confirm with Enter, enter body text, and click outside the body editor to save.
Reload the Note’s creation page, then follow its company relation back to the company. Open Notes and confirm the saved title appears on its card.
Open the company Timeline and click the Note’s creation entry. Without entering a replacement title, click outside the empty Title editor. Reload and observe Untitled while the body remains.
For the Task variant, create a fresh Task, enter a unique title, confirm it with Enter, and open its full record.
Reload that Task page and observe the empty title editor. Select Fields or press Enter without entering a replacement title.
Reload or reopen the Task and confirm the previously saved title has been erased. On a fresh equivalent Task, press Escape instead to confirm the saved name is retained.

The same Note variant also reproduces when creating a standalone Note from Notes at tablet width: save its title with Enter, reload its creation page, then click outside the empty title editor or press Tab to persist the empty title. Pressing Escape instead preserves the saved name.

logicalBugs.explanation: Deleting a Note or Task from a company’s embedded activity view removes its card but leaves the overall Notes or Tasks total unchanged until the view is reopened or refreshed.

rootCause.explanation: Related activities query activity-target connections, whose totalCount is independent of the rendered live activities. Deletion removes activity records/cards without updating that target-query aggregate, which is then published unchanged as the widget header count.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Deleting a Note or Task from a company’s embedded activity view removes its card but leaves the overall Notes or Tasks total unchanged until the view is reopened or refreshed.

sourceBugs.name: Deleting a company-related Note or Task leaves its tab total stale

reproductionPaths.expected: The company Notes or Tasks total should decrease when a related activity is deleted, matching the remaining cards and, for Tasks, the group count.
reproductionPaths.actual: After deleting one of two related Notes or Tasks, its card disappears but the header still shows a total of 2. Task group counts decrease correctly. Deleting the final activity can leave a total of 2 above an empty list. Reopening the tab or reloading corrects the total; the deletion itself succeeds.
reproSteps: Sign in, create a fresh company, and open its full record.
From the company Tasks tab, create two distinctly titled related Tasks.
Open one Task from the embedded view and choose Options > Delete Task.
Without refreshing or switching tabs, compare the remaining cards and group count with the overall Tasks total. One card remains and the group count decreases to 1, while the header remains Tasks 2.
Repeat from the company Notes tab with two distinctly titled related Notes. Open one and choose Options > Delete Note. One card remains, but the header still says Notes 2.
Delete the final activity to observe a stale total above an empty list. Reload or reopen the relevant tab and confirm its total corrects itself.

logicalBugs.explanation: Typing into focused command-menu or navigation records Search on an open Note or Task leaves Search empty and saves the query in the activity body.

rootCause.explanation: ActivityRichTextEditor registers a wildcard hotkey for side-panel focus. Its writing-key handler prevents propagation and inserts a new paragraph into the activity editor without checking whether a search input owns the keystroke.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Typing into focused command-menu or navigation records Search on an open Note or Task leaves Search empty and saves the query in the activity body.

sourceBugs.name: Typing in Search with a Note or Task body editor open inserts and saves the query in its body

reproductionPaths.expected: Typing into focused Search filters its commands or records without changing the open activity body.
reproductionPaths.actual: With the command-menu search focused, typing a query such as Delete Note or Export Note leaves the search empty and inserts that query as activity body text. The unintended text persists after reload. Both Notes and Tasks reproduce; controls with the activity editor absent allow command search to work. Navigation records Search, including tablet/mobile bottom Search, also stays blank and inserts a saved paragraph into the mounted activity body; existing baseline content remains.
reproSteps: Sign in, create a fresh Note with a unique title and body, and open its full record with the body editor visible.
Open the record command menu, click its search input, and type a query such as Delete Note or Export Note.
Observe that the search remains empty while the typed query appears in the Note body.
Close the command menu, allow the body save to complete, then reload and confirm the unintended text remains.
Repeat with a fresh Task and its visible body editor. As a control, open the same activity’s Files tab and verify that command-menu typing stays in the search when the body editor is absent.

Additional verified variation: Use navigation records Search, including bottom Search at tablet/mobile width, with the Note or Task Home body editor mounted. Create a fresh Note with a saved baseline body and open its full record Home tab. At tablet/mobile width, click bottom navigation Search and focus Type anything. Type a distinctive query. Observe the empty Search input and unchanged initial results. Close Search, wait for autosave and reload. Confirm the query was added to the Note body while its baseline remains. Repeat on a second fresh Note and a fresh Task. Control: use navigation Search from the Notes list, a Company record, or the activity Timeline without its editor mounted; the query stays in Search.

logicalBugs.explanation: Viewing a related Person’s or Company’s Tasks tab makes an already saved assignee disappear from the open Task, falsely displaying it as unassigned until reload.

rootCause.explanation: useActivities replaces each activity record-store entry with a shallow activity fetched through a depth-zero target query. The response omits the assignee relation, so opening related Tasks replaces the complete Task with a record lacking the displayed assignee.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Viewing a related Person’s or Company’s Tasks tab makes an already saved assignee disappear from the open Task, falsely displaying it as unassigned until reload.

sourceBugs.name: Opening a related record’s Tasks tab hides the open Task’s saved assignee

reproductionPaths.expected: Opening a related record’s Tasks tab preserves the open Task’s displayed saved assignee.
reproductionPaths.actual: A Task initially displays its saved assignee. After opening a related Person’s Tasks tab in a side panel, the main Task’s Assignee field becomes an empty placeholder. The assignment remains saved, changing Status during the blank display does not clear it, and reloading restores the assignee. The same display failure was reproduced through a related Company’s Tasks tab.
reproSteps: Sign in, create a fresh Task, and open its full record.
Assign an existing workspace member and reload to confirm the assignee remains saved and visible.
Relate an existing Person to the Task and reload. Confirm the assignee is still displayed.
Click the related Person to open their side panel, then select its Tasks tab.
Observe that the original Task’s Assignee field now displays an empty placeholder even though no assignment edit was made.
Reload the Task and confirm the original assignee returns. Opening the Person’s Home or Timeline instead of Tasks preserves the displayed assignee.

logicalBugs.explanation: The Previous Calendar event action can skip adjacent records or remain on the current event when multiple events share the same sort position, while Next traverses them correctly.

rootCause.explanation: Cursor filtering appends an ascending ID tie-breaker when the sort omits ID, but the reversed-order neighbor query reverses only the explicitly supplied fields. Tied-position Previous results are therefore ordered with an inconsistent implicit ID direction.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The Previous Calendar event action can skip adjacent records or remain on the current event when multiple events share the same sort position, while Next traverses them correctly.

sourceBugs.name: Previous Calendar event navigation skips tied-position records or stays on the same event

reproductionPaths.expected: Previous opens the immediately preceding Calendar event in the current view’s ordering, including when records share the same sort position.
reproductionPaths.actual: In a three-event view ordered A, B, C with tied positions, Next visits A, B, C correctly, but Previous from C opens A and skips B. Previous from the first tied event can remain on that event instead of navigating correctly. Seeded later events also jump back to Team Standup rather than the adjacent event. Controls with distinct positions navigate correctly.
reproSteps: Sign in and open Calendar events through the command menu. Use the default ordering, in which seeded events share the same position value.
Open a later event such as Strategic Planning Workshop or Training Session, then choose Navigate to previous Calendar event.
